purpose: Independently inspect whether candidate audio source evidence is present across contrasting authored Minecraft worlds before adding a generic typed Semantic IR audio effect.
method: Parse actual runtime JavaScript extracted from the indicated .mcworld archive with the TypeScript JS AST (ts.createSourceFile). Count CallExpression whose direct property method name equals playSound. This is a syntactic count, NOT receiver type verification, world-audio success, independently scored game design, or executed M-Lazy-Developer parser/IR.
finding: The existing Semantic IR world-effect vocabulary does not include these developer-reference-relevant authored sound attempts. Typed Player/Dimension.playSound can be normalized without source-name, filename, map-genre or historical-example special cases. Other callable playSound aliases remain unresolved unless the existing receiver inference yields a compatible type.
negativeControls: Method spelling playSound alone is not proof of a Minecraft Script API receiver.
An authored sound attempt does not establish audible delivery, a win/loss outcome, or correct phase feedback.
Different map versions and historical samples cannot supply current selected-map gameplay authority.
boundaries: Independent AST source inspection is not the canonical production ScriptMethodCall inference output.
The new typed Semantic IR site is code-only until integrated programmatic inspection is actually run.
No authored world or proprietary source file was committed; only bounded aggregate evidence.
